_meta.description: LLM-generated Critics' Take summaries for shows (concise 1-2 sentence summary, max 280 chars)
_meta.updatePolicy: Regenerate weekly if 3+ new reviews added to any show

two-strangers-bway-2025.text: This modest British rom-com musical charms most critics with its sincerity and Sam Tutty's breakout performance, though some find it lightweight and formulaic. A sleeper hit candidate that prioritizes heart over spectacle.

maybe-happy-ending-2024.text: Critics hail this intimate robot romance as the most original musical in years, praising its visual innovation, emotional depth, and charm. A few find it too slight, but most are enchanted by its tender, human storytelling.

the-outsiders-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this faithful adaptation of the beloved novel, praising its emotional performances and folk score but questioning whether it justifies its existence as a musical beyond nostalgia.

hells-kitchen-2024.text: Critics praise Hell's Kitchen's powerhouse vocals and Alicia Keys' infectious catalog, with standout performances from Maleah Joi Moon and the ensemble. However, many cite a formulaic book and second-act struggles that prevent the jukebox musical from fully soaring.

operation-mincemeat-2025.text: Critics are charmed by this zany British WWII musical's energetic five-person cast and standout ballad "Dear Bill," though some find the frenetic comedy exhausting and too clever by half.

oh-mary-2024.text: Critics hail Cole Escola's irreverent farce as hilariously funny, with most praising its breakneck pace and outrageous reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, profane cabaret wannabe, though a few find it too crude or one-note.

the-great-gatsby-2024.text: Critics find this lavish "Great Gatsby" musical visually stunning but emotionally hollow, prioritizing spectacle over substance. Jordan and Noblezada impress, but the adaptation misses Fitzgerald's deeper themes about class and yearning.

bug-2026.text: Critics praise Letts's psychological thriller as unnervingly timely for our conspiracy-obsessed era, with Carrie Coon delivering a powerhouse performance. The production mostly captivates, though some find it doesn't fully get under the skin.

wicked-2003.text: Critics are divided on Wicked, with many praising the spectacular production values, powerhouse vocals, and Schwartz's score, while others find it overlong and lacking focus. The show's enduring popularity has largely defied mixed initial reviews.

hamilton-2015.text: Critics hail "Hamilton" as a revolutionary masterpiece that transforms American history into thrilling hip-hop theater. Miranda's brilliant writing, inventive staging, and diverse casting create Broadway's most exciting, significant musical in decades.

the-lion-king-1997.text: Critics hail Julie Taymor's staging as a visual marvel and theatrical triumph, with breathtaking puppetry, costumes, and African-inspired design creating an unparalleled spectacle that transcends its Disney origins.

chicago-1996.text: Critics hail the "Chicago" revival as wildly entertaining and remarkably vital, with its stripped-down staging, sharp choreography, and cynical edge feeling more relevant than ever, though celebrity stunt casting varies in quality.

moulin-rouge-2019.text: Critics are divided on this lavish spectacle: many praise its dazzling visuals, energetic performances, and 70-song pop mashup, while others find it exhausting, overstuffed, and emotionally hollow beneath the glitter.

aladdin-2014.text: Critics give Disney's "Aladdin" a mixed-to-positive reception, praising James Monroe Iglehart's scene-stealing Genie and the dazzling spectacle, but finding the show formulaic and lacking the magic of the original film.

hadestown-2019.text: Critics praise Hadestown as a stunning, innovative folk-opera retelling of the Orpheus myth, with gorgeous music and visionary staging by Rachel Chavkin. Some find the story slight or undramatic, but most hail it as a theatrical triumph.

mj-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this estate-approved musical, praising Myles Frost's performance and spectacular choreography while faulting the show for sidestepping Jackson's controversies in favor of slick hagiography.

six-2021.text: Critics praise SIX as an energetic, catchy pop concert musical that gives Henry VIII's wives their own stories. The 80-minute show earns acclaim for its infectious songs and girl-power message, though some find the book thin.

book-of-mormon-2011.text: Critics hail "The Book of Mormon" as hilariously irreverent yet surprisingly sweet, with sharp satire, catchy songs, and expert craftsmanship that affirms faith while skewering religious fanaticism.

and-juliet-2022.text: Critics are divided on this pop-fueled feminist reimagining of Shakespeare. While Max Martin's catchy hits and energetic performances win over many, others find the messaging heavy-handed and the plot thin, making it more teenage dream than substantial theater.

oedipus-2025.text: Critics hail Robert Icke's modern "Oedipus" as a riveting political thriller, with Strong and Manville delivering electrifying performances. Most praise its sleek urgency and contemporary resonance, though some find it clever rather than profound.

harry-potter-2021.text: Critics praise the spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions but find the story overstuffed and best suited for Potter devotees. The production dazzles with technical wizardry, though some feel disconnected by the plot-heavy narrative.

mamma-mia-2025.text: Critics find "Mamma Mia!" a flawed but irresistibly fun guilty pleasure, with ABBA's infectious hits overpowering a silly plot and basic production. Audiences eat it up, even if it's far from high art.

stranger-things-2024.text: Critics are divided on this FX-heavy prequel: some praise its jaw-dropping spectacle and theatrical imagination, while others find it an exhausting, confusing theme park ride that prioritizes tech over substance and heart.

cabaret-2024.text: Critics are divided on this immersive revival: some praise Redmayne's mesmerizing Emcee and the stunning theater transformation, while others find the spectacle overwrought and the production stagnant beneath its lavish surface.

stereophonic-2024.text: Critics hail David Adjmi's three-hour studio drama as a masterpiece of hyper-naturalistic theater, praising its immersive 1970s design, authentic performances, and Will Butler's original songs, though some find its length exhausting.

water-for-elephants-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this circus-set musical adaptation: the acrobatic spectacle and authentic circus elements dazzle, but the conventional story and forgettable score disappoint.

suffs-2024.text: Critics are mixed on Shaina Taub's suffrage musical, praising its rousing score and strong performances but finding it overlong and more educational than dramatic. The show earns points for timely relevance and ensemble work, though some call it preachy.

the-notebook-2024.text: Critics are divided on this tearjerker musical adaptation, with some praising Ingrid Michaelson's score and strong performances while others find it emotionally manipulative and thinly drawn. It delivers the expected weepy moments but rarely transcends its source material.

marjorie-prime-2025.text: Critics praise this timely AI drama for its emotional intelligence and superb ensemble led by 96-year-old June Squibb, though some find it more intellectually engaging than deeply moving, with its ideas occasionally overshadowing its heart.

liberation-2025.text: Critics largely embrace Wohl's sophisticated memory play about 1970s feminists, praising its superb ensemble cast and timely relevance. Some find it structurally uneven, but most laud its humor, emotional depth, and bold second act.

boop-2025.text: Critics are mixed on this polished but generic musical, though nearly all praise Jasmine Amy Rogers' star-making Broadway debut. The show offers dazzling spectacle and escapist fun, but many question why it needed to exist.

queen-versailles-2025.text: Kristin Chenoweth dazzles in this Stephen Schwartz musical, but critics find the show as unfinished as its titular mansion—a tonally confused spectacle that can't decide whether to satirize or celebrate excess, leaving audiences with empty opulence.

death-becomes-her-2024.text: Critics are divided on this campy musical adaptation, but most agree Megan Hilty and Jennifer Simard's powerhouse performances elevate the splashy spectacle, even when the show lacks emotional depth.

buena-vista-social-club-2025.text: Critics praise the intoxicating Cuban music and vibrant dance performances, but find the book wispy and clichéd. The show works better as a concert than a fully realized musical, though its infectious energy wins over most reviewers.

ragtime-2025.text: Critics hail this stripped-down revival as powerfully relevant and magnificently sung, with Joshua Henry's performance earning particular praise. A few find the minimalist staging overly presentational, but most agree the production resonates urgently today.

chess-2025.text: Critics remain divided on this revival: the powerhouse vocals and infectious ABBA score earn praise, but the notoriously messy book still frustrates, leaving Chess an entertaining yet fundamentally flawed spectacle.

just-in-time-2025.text: Jonathan Groff delivers a dazzling, Tony-worthy performance in this Bobby Darin bio-musical, though critics split on the formulaic book. The intimate staging and showmanship thrill, but dialogue scenes drag when the music stops.

the-roommate-2024.text: Critics find Farrow and LuPone's star power elevates Silverman's slight, predictable odd-couple comedy about mismatched roommates, though the thin script struggles to match its performers' considerable talents.

our-town-2024.text: Critics largely praise this moving revival, with Jim Parsons earning acclaim as the Stage Manager in Kenny Leon's swift, diverse production. Some find it faithful but unexceptional, unable to match David Cromer's legendary 2009 staging.

back-to-the-future-2023.text: Critics are divided on this faithful film adaptation: the DeLorean's spectacular effects and technical wizardry dazzle, but many find the score forgettable and the production more theme park attraction than meaningful musical theater.

all-out-2025.text: Critics find "All Out" a mildly entertaining but unambitious showcase of Simon Rich stories and music that feels random and overpriced, with marketing criticized as misleading about the show's actual content.

real-women-have-curves-2025.text: Critics warmly embrace this joyful, heart-filled musical about Latina immigrants in an LA dress factory, praising its body-positive title number and vibrant energy, though some find the coming-of-age story predictable and its themes uneven.

redwood-2025.text: Critics find Menzel's powerhouse vocals and stunning visual design impressive, but the thin, formulaic story about grief fails to resonate emotionally, leaving the spectacular tree as the show's most memorable element.

days-of-wine-and-roses-2024.text: Critics largely praise O'Hara and d'Arcy James's powerhouse performances and Guettel's sophisticated jazz-inflected score, though some question whether the bleak subject matter of alcoholism suits the musical form.

harmony-2023.text: Barry Manilow's long-gestating musical about the Nazi-era Comedian Harmonists earns mixed reviews. Critics praise the beautiful vocal harmonies and timely anti-Semitism themes, but fault the formulaic book, uneven pacing, and heavy-handed dramatics.

here-lies-love-2023.text: David Byrne's immersive disco musical about Imelda Marcos dazzles with its innovative staging and infectious score, transforming Broadway into a pulsating nightclub, though critics are divided on whether its political complexities get lost in the party atmosphere.

how-to-dance-in-ohio-2023.text: Critics praise the groundbreaking casting of autistic actors but find the musical itself uneven, with a forgettable score and overly earnest book undermining the cast's authentic, winning performances.

illinoise-2024.text: Justin Peck's dance-theater adaptation of Sufjan Stevens' album earns widespread praise as a gorgeous, moving meditation on love and loss, though some find its narrative unclear or emotionally distant.

lempicka-2024.text: Critics are divided on this bio-musical about Art Deco painter Tamara de Lempicka. While some praise Espinosa's performance and striking visuals, most find the show overstuffed, tonally uneven, and struggling with a clunky book that never captures its subject's complexity.

once-upon-a-one-more-time-2023.text: Critics are split on this Britney Spears jukebox musical about feminist fairy tale princesses. Fans praise its infectious energy, sharp choreography, and pure fun, while detractors find it shallow, pandering, and overly long despite catchy songs.

heart-of-rock-and-roll-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this Huey Lewis jukebox musical, with most finding it predictable and formulaic but surprisingly fun. The witty book, energetic performances, and unpretentious '80s nostalgia win over many, though some dismiss it as lightweight fluff.

gutenberg-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this meta-musical parody: Gad and Rannells earn praise for their chemistry and comic timing, but many find the thin premise exhausting over two hours, with jokes that wear thin despite genuine laughs.

merrily-we-roll-along-2023.text: Critics hail this revival as a triumphant vindication of Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop. Maria Friedman's direction and the chemistry of leads Groff, Radcliffe, and Mendez finally unlock the show's emotional core, making it a palpable Broadway hit at last.

spamalot-2023.text: Critics mostly embrace this energetic revival, praising its talented comedic cast (especially Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer) and timeless Python silliness, though some find certain jokes dated and the production lacking fresh vision.

the-whos-tommy-2024.text: McAnuff's electrifying revival of The Who's rock opera delivers sensory overload with stunning visuals and powerhouse performances, though critics split on whether its convoluted plot and excess enhance or overwhelm the iconic music.

the-wiz-2024.text: Critics are divided on this "Wiz" revival: some praise its soulful energy and strong cast, while others find it a disappointing, cheap-looking production that fails to capture the original's magic.

grey-house-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this atmospheric Broadway horror play. While Mantello's direction and the committed cast earn praise for creating genuine scares, many find the plot confusing and the pacing sluggish, with themes that don't fully cohere.

i-need-that-2023.text: Critics find Rebeck's hoarding comedy thin and predictable despite DeVito's charismatic performance. The play feels like a sitcom stretched too long, with pat insights and repetitive scenes, though DeVito brings humor and heart to underwritten material.

jajas-african-hair-braiding-2023.text: Critics warmly embrace Bioh's vibrant workplace comedy, praising its sparkling ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and celebration of West African immigrant life in Harlem. Some note the dramatic ending feels awkward, but most find it wildly entertaining.

just-for-us-2023.text: Alex Edelman's solo comedy about infiltrating a white nationalist meeting earns widespread acclaim for its sharp wit and timely relevance, with critics praising his quickfire delivery and ability to balance hilarity with uncomfortable truths about antisemitism.

mary-jane-2024.text: Critics praise Amy Herzog's intimate drama and Rachel McAdams' authentic Broadway debut as a mother caring for her severely ill son, calling it deeply moving yet never sentimental, though the emotionally grueling subject matter proves difficult for some.

mother-play-2024.text: Vogel's autobiographical memory play earns mixed reviews: Lange delivers a magnetic, commanding performance, but the predictable story feels incomplete and emotionally distant despite moments of humor and poignant staging.

patriots-2024.text: Critics praise Michael Stuhlbarg's commanding performance as oligarch Boris Berezovsky, but find Peter Morgan's Putin drama more successful as gripping history lesson than insightful political theater, with an uneven structure that loses steam.

prayer-for-the-french-republic-2024.text: Harmon's ambitious three-hour epic about a French Jewish family grappling with antisemitism earns strong praise for its emotional power and timely resonance, though some critics find it overlong and heavy-handed in its debates.

the-cottage-2023.text: Critics are sharply divided on this Noël Coward-style farce: some find it a delightfully silly romp with strong performances, while others dismiss it as strained, vulgar, and lacking the wit of true drawing-room comedy.

the-shark-is-broken-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this behind-the-scenes comedy about the making of "Jaws." While performances earn praise, many find the script too slight and repetitive, though some appreciate its exploration of male ego and father-son dynamics.

an-enemy-of-the-people-2024.text: Ibsen's classic receives a timely, muscular revival with Strong and Imperioli delivering intense performances, though critics split on whether Gold's production fully realizes its contemporary relevance or veers into heavy-handed territory.

appropriate-2023.text: Critics hail Jacobs-Jenkins' searing family drama as a modern masterpiece, praising Neugebauer's riveting direction and a powerhouse ensemble led by Sarah Paulson that brilliantly balances dark comedy with unflinching examinations of racism and legacy.

doubt-2024.text: Shanley's Pulitzer-winning script remains sharp and relevant, though this revival draws mixed reactions on execution. Ryan and Schreiber lead a strong cast, but some critics find the production underpowered where it should electrify.

purlie-victorious-2023.text: Critics hail this first Broadway revival as hilarious, timely, and sharply satirical, with standout performances from Leslie Odom Jr. and especially Kara Young. Kenny Leon's brisk direction keeps Davis's 1961 comedy feeling urgent and relevant.

uncle-vanya-2024.text: Mixed reviews greet this star-studded revival, with critics divided on whether the modern translation and Steve Carell's performance successfully revitalize Chekhov or fail to cohere, finding comedy but often missing emotional depth.

titanique-2026.text: Critics find this campy Celine Dion-scored parody of the Titanic film outrageously funny and deliriously absurd, praising its irreverent humor and commitment to over-the-top performances, though some note it works best for devoted fans of the movie and Dion.

home-2024.text: Kenny Leon's poignant revival of Samm-Art Williams' 1979 play earns praise for Tory Kittles' powerful performance and poetic language, though some critics find the dated storytelling uneven and the dense vernacular challenging to parse.

job-2024.text: Critics are divided on this taut 80-minute thriller about a viral video victim holding her therapist at gunpoint. Many praise the electrifying performances and internet-age commentary, though some find the premise implausible and the tension unsustainable.

once-upon-a-mattress-2024.text: Sutton Foster dazzles in a role she was born to play, delivering a tour-de-force comic performance that elevates this charming but bare-bones Encores! transfer, even if the production itself feels more dutiful than inspired.

the-hills-of-california-2024.text: Critics praise Butterworth's family drama for stellar performances, especially Laura Donnelly's tour-de-force dual role, though some find its three-hour runtime meandering. The play's haunting atmosphere and emotional depth resonate, even if it lacks "The Ferryman's" grandeur.

mcneal-2024.text: Critics find Akhtar's AI-focused play muddled and unfocused despite Downey Jr.'s magnetic Broadway debut. The timely premise about artificial intelligence and creativity sparks interest, but most agree the drama lacks emotional depth and narrative clarity.

yellow-face-2024.text: Critics praise Hwang's meta-theatrical comedy as brilliant, funny, and surprisingly relevant, with Daniel Dae Kim excelling in the lead. The play masterfully blends personal confession with sharp social commentary on race and identity.

sunset-boulevard-2024.text: Jamie Lloyd's stripped-down, camera-heavy revival electrifies with Nicole Scherzinger's powerhouse Broadway debut as Norma Desmond, though some find the bold staging gimmicky and relentlessly intense.

left-on-tenth-2024.text: Critics find this memoir adaptation charmingly performed by Margulies but dramatically inert, with most citing surface-level storytelling that works better on the page than stage, though some praise its warmth and intimacy.

romeo-juliet-2024.text: Sam Gold's Gen Z-targeted revival divides critics: Connor and Zegler show strong chemistry, but the hyperactive, club-kid aesthetic and gimmicky modernization often overshadow Shakespeare's text, resulting in style over substance.

a-wonderful-world-the-louis-armstrong-mu.text: Iglehart shines as Satchmo with charisma and vocal prowess, but the jukebox bio-musical struggles to balance celebration with depth, cramming in nearly 30 songs while never fully exploring what made Armstrong a legend.

tammy-faye-2024.text: Critics find "Tammy Faye" messy and tonally confused, struggling between camp and sincerity. Katie Brayben's powerhouse performance earns praise, but Elton John's score and the muddled book disappoint in this uneven British import.

elf-2024.text: Critics find this crowd-pleasing revival delivers holiday cheer and Grey Henson's winning performance, though the musical itself remains mediocre with forgettable songs and thin plotting that wears out its one-joke premise.

swept-away-2024.text: Critics are divided on this dark Avett Brothers musical about shipwrecked sailors. While the folk-rock score earns widespread praise and the cast impresses, many find the 90-minute show too rushed and dramatically uneven to fully connect.

cult-of-love-2024.text: Critics find Headland's dysfunctional family Christmas drama caustically funny and well-acted, though some feel it's overstuffed with issues. The starry cast and sharp writing earn praise, but the play occasionally veers into melodrama.

eureka-day-2024.text: Critics praise this sharp satire of progressive politics as hilarious and timely, with standout ensemble work and a legendary Zoom scene. Some find it uncomfortable or unbalanced, but most laud its wit in skewering well-meaning liberals.

gypsy-2024.text: Critics hail McDonald's grounded, emotionally intelligent Rose as a revelation, bringing fresh nuance and heartbreaking vulnerability to the iconic role. Wolfe's revival mostly honors the classic while letting its star shine in a performance many call career-defining.

all-in-comedy-about-love-2024.text: Simon Rich's star-studded staged reading of comic short stories delivers gentle laughs but divides critics on whether it justifies Broadway prices, with some charmed by its wit and others dismissing it as slight.

english-2025.text: Toossi's Pulitzer-winning play about Iranian students learning English earns widespread praise for its thoughtful exploration of language and identity.

purpose-2025.text: Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another sharp family drama with scorching dialogue and excellent performances, though critics note the ambitious second act doesn't quite match the brilliant first's momentum.

othello-2025.text: Star power can't save this underpowered "Othello." Critics find Washington and Gyllenhaal miscast in Kenny Leon's bland, directionless production that mistakes celebrity for substance, leaving audiences with little drama beyond the $900 ticket prices.

the-picture-of-dorian-gray-2025.text: Sarah Snook delivers a virtuosic performance playing 26 characters in this technically dazzling adaptation, though critics are divided on whether the innovative camera work and video screens enhance or overwhelm Wilde's story.

glengarry-glen-ross-2025.text: Mamet's masterpiece crackles with a starry cast (Culkin, Odenkirk, Burr) delivering sharp performances, though critics split on whether this revival justifies another trip to the well. Many cite miscasting and an oversized venue that dilutes the play's tension.

good-night-and-good-luck-2025.text: Critics are mixed on Clooney's Broadway debut, praising its timely urgency and his charismatic performance as Murrow, but many find the adaptation too faithful to the film, resulting in a well-intentioned yet dramatically flat theatrical experience.

the-last-five-years-2025.text: Brown's beloved score shines with Warren's powerhouse performance, but this overproduced Broadway debut feels emotionally hollow and visually cluttered, struggling to capture the intimate two-hander's delicate essence.

stephen-sondheims-old-friends-2025.text: Critics are divided on this Sondheim revue: some praise the stellar cast led by Bernadette Peters and call it a joyous feast, while others find it overly long, exhausting, and lacking the dramatic context that made the songs great.

john-proctor-is-the-villain-2025.text: Critics praise this timely, sharply written #MeToo-era reimagining of "The Crucible" for its authentic teen voices and stellar ensemble led by Sadie Sink, though some find it heavy-handed in tackling feminist themes.

floyd-collins-2025.text: Critics praise Guettel's beautiful score and Jordan's performance, but remain divided on whether this chamber musical about a trapped cave explorer succeeds on Broadway's larger stage, with some finding it moving and others cold.

pirates-the-penzance-musical-2025.text: This New Orleans-set reimagining of Gilbert & Sullivan's operetta charms most critics with its playful energy and standout performances, though purists may balk at the liberties taken with the classic material.

dead-outlaw-2025.text: Critics praise this darkly inventive musical about outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre afterlife, lauding Yazbek and Della Penna's rockabilly score, Durand's remarkable corpse performance, and Cromer's sharp direction, though some find the macabre premise uneven.

the-kite-runner-2022.text: Mixed reviews greet this faithful adaptation of Hosseini's bestseller, with critics praising its emotional story but faulting excessive narration over action and a lead performance that rarely soars.

into-the-woods-2022.text: This stripped-down revival earns acclaim for its stellar cast and emotional clarity, letting Sondheim's score shine. Critics praise the performances and direction, though some find the minimalist staging unremarkable.

leopoldstadt-2022.text: Critics hail Stoppard's deeply personal Holocaust drama as a powerful departure from his usual cerebral style, praising its emotional devastation and sweeping family portrait. Some find the large cast overwhelming, but most consider it among his finest works.

cost-of-living-2022.text: Majok's Pulitzer-winning drama earns strong praise for its unsentimental portrayal of disability and intimacy, anchored by exceptional performances. Critics laud its emotional power and refusal to sentimentalize, though some find it plotless.

1776-2022.text: This revival's diverse casting brings fresh energy to the 1969 musical, with critics praising the talented ensemble and contemporary relevance, though many find the production overly heavy-handed and the directorial choices distractingly literal-minded.

death-of-a-salesman-2022.text: Pierce and Clarke deliver powerful performances in this historic revival featuring a Black Loman family, adding new dimensions to Miller's classic. Critics praise the leads' emotional depth, though some find directorial choices distracting.

the-piano-lesson-2022.text: Critics praise this star-studded revival's strong performances and rich design, though some find LaTanya Richardson Jackson's direction uneven and the supernatural elements overdone. The cast honors Wilson's text with power and authenticity.

topdog-underdog-2022.text: Parks' Pulitzer-winning play crackles with renewed vitality in this electrifying revival, powered by powerhouse performances from Hawkins and Abdul-Mateen II that bring fresh urgency to the timeless drama of brotherhood and survival.

walking-with-ghosts-2022.text: Critics are divided on Byrne's memoir adaptation: admirers praise his masterful storytelling and charisma, while detractors find the staging loose and question why this intimate material needs a Broadway production.

almost-famous-2022.text: Critics are divided on this rock musical adaptation, with many finding it a pleasant but sanitized retelling that captures the film's spirit but lacks its emotional depth and edge.

kimberly-akimbo-2022.text: Critics hail this quirky musical as a small miracle that balances heartbreak and humor with remarkable tonal precision.

take-me-out-2022.text: This revival of Greenberg's 2003 Tony winner feels both timely and dated, elevated by superb performances from Ferguson and Williams. The play's wit and themes resonate, though some find it overlong and struggling with dramatic balance.

mike-birbiglia-the-old-man-and-the-pool-.text: Birbiglia's latest solo show earns strong praise for his masterful storytelling that transforms middle-aged anxiety and mortality into hilarious, deeply personal, and surprisingly moving comedy through his signature circular narrative style.

a-christmas-carol-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this technically dazzling production, praising Jefferson Mays' virtuosic 50-character performance and spectacular stagecraft, but some find it overly reliant on spectacle at the expense of emotional depth.

kpop-2022.text: Critics find KPOP delivers electrifying choreography and stellar performances, but struggles with a thin, underdeveloped book that undermines the spectacle, resulting in more concert than fully realized musical theater.

aint-no-mo-2022.text: Critics largely praise Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire as a bold, provocative comedy tackling Black American life with fearless humor and pain, though some find it uneven and more sketch-like than cohesive.

a-beautiful-noise-the-neil-diamond-music.text: Critics find this Neil Diamond jukebox musical delivers crowd-pleasing hits with strong vocal performances, particularly from lead Nick Fradiani, but suffers from a weak book and therapy-session framing device that appeals mainly to devoted fans.

ohio-state-murders-2022.text: Critics praise Audra McDonald's mesmerizing, emotionally devastating performance in Adrienne Kennedy's belated Broadway debut, a concentrated 75-minute memory play about racial violence. Reception is largely positive, though some find the production overly reverent.

some-like-it-hot-2022.text: Critics largely embrace this energetic adaptation as a crowd-pleasing throwback, praising Casey Nicholaw's dazzling choreography and updated gender politics, though some find the score derivative and the production occasionally exhausting in its efforts to dazzle.

the-collaboration-2022.text: Mixed reviews praise Bettany and Pope's magnetic performances as Warhol and Basquiat, but find McCarten's play superficial and dramatically inert, better at exploring their personal bond than offering fresh insights into their art.

between-riverside-and-crazy-2022.text: Guirgis's Pulitzer winner earns strong reviews for Henderson's powerhouse performance and vibrant dialogue, though some find the plot uneven. Critics praise its compassionate character study and social commentary about gentrification and survival in New York.

pictures-from-home-2023.text: Lane, Burstein, and Wanamaker deliver strong performances in this adaptation of Larry Sultan's photo memoir, but critics find the play repetitive and underdeveloped, with most praising the acting while faulting the thin, diffuse narrative.

a-dolls-house-2023.text: Jamie Lloyd's radically stripped-down revival divides critics: some praise Chastain's fierce performance and Herzog's adaptation as bold and laser-focused, while others find the minimalist approach static and overly austere, reducing Ibsen to a lifeless reading.

parade-2023.text: Critics hail this revival of "Parade" as urgent and devastatingly powerful, with exceptional performances from its leads and Jason Robert Brown's stunning score elevating the tragic Leo Frank story into essential, timely theater.

bob-fosses-dancin-2023.text: The revival dazzles with exceptional dancers executing Fosse's iconic choreography, but critics find it lacks narrative coherence and feels more like a glitzy museum piece than vital theater.

bad-cinderella-2023.text: Critics largely pan this Lloyd Webber musical as a confused, overstuffed mess that fails to meaningfully update the fairy tale, though some praise his melodies and Carolee Carmello's scene-stealing stepmother performance.

sweeney-todd-2023.text: Critics hail this full-scale revival as a triumphant return for Sondheim's masterpiece, praising Groban and Ashford's powerful performances and the lush 26-piece orchestra, though some find the production plays it safe rather than going for maximum shock.

life-of-pi-2023.text: Critics praise "Life of Pi" as a visual spectacle with stunning puppetry and stagecraft, particularly the lifelike Bengal tiger. While the technical achievements and lead performance dazzle, some find the narrative less engaging than the theatrical wizardry.

shucked-2023.text: Critics find "Shucked" an aggressively corny but surprisingly charming musical comedy that delivers relentless puns and dad jokes alongside a country score. Most praise its infectious energy and committed cast, though some find the humor exhausting and the plot thin.

fat-ham-2023.text: Critics praise this Pulitzer-winning Hamlet reimagining as raucously funny and deeply moving, with its queer Black protagonist at a Southern barbecue. Most laud Ijames' wit and emotional depth, though some find it occasionally strains under its ambitions.

camelot-2023.text: Sorkin's revised "Camelot" divides critics: some praise Soo's performance and the sumptuous production, but many find it overly dark, joyless, and dramatically inert, with the removal of magic draining the show's heart and fun.

peter-pan-goes-wrong-2023.text: Critics find this slapstick comedy delivers precisely choreographed chaos and family-friendly laughs, though some note the relentless physical gags grow repetitive over two hours. Most praise the technical precision and controlled mayhem.

the-thanksgiving-play-2023.text: FastHorse's satire of performative wokeness delivers sharp laughs skewering well-meaning white liberals, but critics are split on whether its 2015-era humor feels dated and whether it offers meaningful solutions beyond roasting its targets.

prima-facie-2023.text: Critics hail Jodie Comer's "tour de force" Broadway debut as extraordinary and commanding, though some find Suzie Miller's #MeToo legal thriller overly schematic or didactic. The performance transcends any reservations about the play's structure.

good-night-oscar-2023.text: Hayes delivers a tour-de-force performance as Oscar Levant that earns raves, but critics are divided on Wright's biographical play, with some finding it a captivating character study and others calling it exposition-heavy Wikipedia theater.

summer-1976-2023.text: Linney and Hecht deliver masterful performances in Auburn's gentle, nostalgic two-hander, though critics find the play itself thin and uneventful—a pleasant but minor work elevated by its stars' acting prowess.

new-york-new-york-2023.text: Critics find this Kander and Ebb musical overstuffed and unfocused, struggling between tourist-friendly spectacle and serious themes about racism.

the-sign-in-sidney-brusteins-window-2023.text: Isaac and Brosnahan electrify Hansberry's sprawling, unfinished play about 1960s idealism, but critics split on whether the verbose, overstuffed script coheres into a satisfying whole despite the stellar performances and timely themes.

pass-over-2021.text: Critics hail "Pass Over" as urgent, powerful theater that marks a watershed moment for Broadway's return. Nwandu's Beckett-inspired examination of Black experience in America earns praise for its bold relevance and strong performances.

waitress-2021.text: Critics find "Waitress" a sweet, crowd-pleasing musical elevated by Jessie Mueller's stellar performance and Sara Bareilles' appealing pop score, though some fault the broad characterizations and overly familiar plot that doesn't always justify its tonal shifts.

lackawanna-blues-2021.text: Santiago-Hudson delivers a virtuosic performance in this warmly nostalgic solo show, inhabiting two dozen characters from his childhood with impressive skill, though some critics find the autobiographical storytelling more self-indulgent than transcendent.

chicken-and-biscuits-2021.text: This warmhearted family funeral comedy charms with strong performances and genuine laughs, but critics note its formulaic sitcom structure, uneven pacing, and tendency to lurch between broad humor and melodrama undercut its appeal.

is-this-a-room-2021.text: Critics hail this verbatim FBI transcript as gripping, anxiety-inducing theater that transforms bureaucratic document into psychological thriller. Emily Davis's raw performance and Tina Satter's taut direction create riveting drama from mundane interrogation.

thoughts-of-a-colored-man-2021.text: Scott's timely exploration of Black masculinity through seven Brooklyn men earns praise for authentic performances and urgent themes, though critics find its episodic structure more a collection of monologues than fully integrated drama.

the-lehman-trilogy-2021.text: Critics hail this epic as a theatrical triumph, with Mendes' direction and three extraordinary actors transforming 164 years of financial history into gripping, accessible drama, though some find it glosses over moral complexities.

dana-h-2021.text: Critics hail this formally audacious work as unlike anything on Broadway, with O'Connell's tour-de-force lip-synced performance creating an unsettling, mesmerizing theatrical experience that blurs documentary and drama.

caroline-or-change-2021.text: Critics hail Sharon D Clarke's towering performance in this ambitious, uneven musical. While some find Kushner and Tesori's complex score and storytelling transcendent, others cite pacing issues and a lecturing tone that undercuts emotional impact.

diana-the-musical-2021.text: Critics largely pan Diana as a tone-deaf, superficial musical with weak songs and tasteless lyrics that reduces a tragic figure to tabloid fodder, though some find it entertainingly campy in its badness.

trouble-in-mind-2021.text: Childress's 1955 backstage satire about racism in theater finally reaches Broadway 65+ years late and feels urgently relevant. Critics praise its sharp insights and LaChanze's commanding performance, calling it a mandatory, timely stop.

clydes-2021.text: Lynn Nottage's warm comedy-drama about ex-cons finding redemption in a truck-stop sandwich shop earns praise for its humor, heart, and powerhouse performances from Uzo Aduba and ensemble, though some critics find it occasionally uneven or overstuffed.

slave-play-2021.text: Harris's provocative exploration of race, sex, and power divides critics: many praise its bold confrontation of America's racial legacy and explosive theatricality, while others find it overwritten and more shocking than dramatically coherent.

company-2021.text: Marianne Elliott's gender-flipped revival feels fresh and vital, with critics praising its inventive staging and Patti LuPone's showstopping "Ladies Who Lunch," though opinion splits on whether Katrina Lenk's Bobbie has the vocal power and vulnerability the role demands.

flying-over-sunset-2021.text: Critics find this LSD-themed musical about Cary Grant, Aldous Huxley, and Clare Boothe Luce visually stunning but dramatically inert—a boring trip that fails to soar despite strong performances from Tony Yazbeck and impressive production design.

skeleton-crew-2022.text: Morisseau's compassionate drama about Detroit auto workers facing economic uncertainty earns praise for its authentic sense of place and strong ensemble, led by Phylicia Rashad's commanding performance, though some find it stronger on atmosphere than dramatic tension.

the-music-man-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this starry revival: Hugh Jackman and Sutton Foster dazzle with undeniable chemistry and charisma, but the lavish production often feels safe and flat, failing to fully recapture the magic of the beloved classic.

plaza-suite-2022.text: Parker and Broderick bring charm and chemistry to Simon's dated 1968 triptych, delivering crowd-pleasing laughs despite material that feels increasingly out of touch with modern sensibilities and #MeToo-era concerns.

paradise-square-2022.text: Critics find Paradise Square overstuffed and unfocused despite noble intentions, though Joaquina Kalukango's powerhouse performance and Bill T. Jones's thrilling choreography earn widespread praise.

beetlejuice-2022.text: Critics find "Beetlejuice" a visually spectacular, high-energy spectacle with strong performances and impressive design, though opinions split on its relentless sensory overload and forgettable score.

birthday-candles-2022.text: Critics are divided on this life-spanning dramedy, with many finding Haidle's 90-year birthday ritual concept manipulative and overstuffed with clichés, though Messing's tour-de-force performance and Jones's inventive set design earn consistent praise.

american-buffalo-2022.text: Critics are mixed on this Mamet revival, praising the powerhouse performances from Rockwell, Fishburne and Criss while questioning whether the 1975 play's profane poetry still resonates or feels dated in 2022.

the-minutes-2022.text: Letts' slow-burn satire of small-town politics builds to a shocking revelation about America's mythologized history. Critics praise the crackling dialogue and disturbing power, though some find the ending heavy-handed and the play less timely after pandemic delays.

how-i-learned-to-drive-2022.text: Vogel's Pulitzer-winning drama about grooming and abuse remains powerfully relevant 25 years later, with critics praising Parker and Morse's "extraordinary" performances in roles they originated, though some find the production overly cautious.

for-colored-girls-who-have-considered-su.text: Critics praise this revival of Shange's groundbreaking choreopoem as urgent and powerfully performed, with Camille A. Brown's exquisite choreography breathing fresh life into the work, though some find it occasionally lacking nuance or showing its age.

hangmen-2022.text: McDonagh's darkly comic thriller about England's last hangman delivers mordant wit and gallows humor, though critics split on whether the thin plot and recycled themes live up to his best work.

funny-girl-2022.text: Critics are divided on this revival: Lea Michele earns raves for her powerhouse vocals and star turn, while Beanie Feldstein received mixed reviews for lacking vocal strength despite her charm and comic timing.

the-skin-of-our-teeth-2022.text: Blain-Cruz's ambitious revival of Wilder's rarely-performed play divides critics with its spectacular design and chaotic energy. While some praise its urgency and emotional power, others find it overlong, uneven, and unable to overcome the text's dated elements.

a-strange-loop-2022.text: Critics hail this Pulitzer-winning meta-musical as a bold, brilliant game-changer that pushes Broadway's boundaries with raw honesty and innovative storytelling, though its explicit content and uncompromising intensity may polarize audiences.

mr-saturday-night-2022.text: Crystal charms with impeccable comic timing, but critics find the musical itself a mixed bag—overlong, schmaltzy, and saddled with forgettable songs that feel more like a play with music than a fully integrated show.

macbeth-2022.text: Critics are divided on this "Macbeth," with many finding Sam Gold's modern staging uneven and underdeveloped despite strong performances from Daniel Craig and Ruth Negga. The production feels more like a chamber piece than epic tragedy.

girl-from-the-north-country-2022.text: Dylan's songs beautifully underscore McPherson's Depression-era drama, creating a haunting anti-jukebox musical. Critics praise the stellar cast and atmospheric storytelling, though some find the narrative overstuffed or the integration uneven.

mrs-doubtfire-2021.text: Critics are mixed on this faithful film adaptation, praising Rob McClure's tour de force performance but finding the show dated, uninspired, and lacking theatrical magic beyond competent execution.

frankie-and-johnny-in-the-clair-de-lune-.text: McDonald and Shannon deliver powerhouse performances in this McNally revival, though critics split on whether the 1987 play feels dated. Most praise the stars' chemistry and comic timing, but some find the second act repetitious and the central romance unconvincing.

betrayal-2019.text: Jamie Lloyd's stripped-down revival of Pinter's reverse-chronology infidelity drama earns strong praise for its surgical precision and emotional depth, with standout performances from Hiddleston, Ashton, and Cox in a spare, haunting production.

the-height-of-the-storm-2019.text: Pryce and Atkins deliver stunning, transcendent performances that elevate Zeller's puzzle-box meditation on aging and memory, though critics split on whether the overly clever, disorienting structure is deeply moving or frustratingly thin.

the-great-society-2019.text: Brian Cox delivers a powerful performance as LBJ, but this overstuffed sequel to "All the Way" struggles under the weight of too many events and characters, resulting in a history lesson that's more dutiful than dramatically compelling.

linda-vista-2019.text: Letts' character study of a toxic, middle-aged divorced man divides critics: some praise its dark humor and unflinching honesty, while others question whether this self-absorbed protagonist merits three hours of attention.

the-rose-tattoo-2019.text: Tomei delivers a committed performance in this uneven revival that struggles to balance Williams' mix of comedy and drama. Critics are divided on Cullman's broad direction and campy staging choices, with many finding the production miscalibrated.

the-lightning-thief-2019.text: Critics are divided on this energetic YA adaptation, with some praising its colorful spirit and devoted fanbase appeal, while others find it a thin, overly loud misfire that fails to capture Broadway-worthy magic.

the-sound-inside-2019.text: Critics praise Mary-Louise Parker's extraordinary performance in Adam Rapp's cerebral two-hander, though some find the literary thriller too bookish or question its fit in the large Studio 54 theater.

tina-2019.text: Adrienne Warren delivers a powerhouse, Tony-worthy performance that electrifies this otherwise formulaic jukebox bio-musical. Critics agree Warren's stunning vocals and charisma transcend the show's by-the-book storytelling and clunky book.

the-inheritance-2019.text: Critics praise this ambitious 6+ hour epic about gay men grappling with AIDS legacy and intergenerational connection, calling it moving and important despite excessive length. Strong performances elevate Lopez's sprawling, sometimes indulgent drama.

a-christmas-carol-2019.text: Jack Thorne's adaptation earns mostly positive reviews for its fresh take on the classic, with Campbell Scott's compelling Scrooge and immersive staging praised, though some critics find it dour and question its departures from tradition.

jagged-little-pill-2019.text: Critics find this Alanis Morissette jukebox musical ambitious but overstuffed, tackling timely issues like addiction and sexual assault with earnest performances. While some praise its emotional power and strong cast, others criticize its contrived plot and heavy-handed approach.

my-name-is-lucy-barton-2020.text: Linney delivers a luminous, masterful performance that elevates a literary adaptation critics find too static for the stage. Most praise her skill, but many question whether this introspective novel works theatrically.

a-soldiers-play-2020.text: Fuller's Pulitzer winner makes a powerful, belated Broadway debut in Leon's riveting revival, led by Grier and Underwood. Critics praise the gripping murder mystery's urgent relevance and strong ensemble, though some find it occasionally heavy-handed.

grand-horizons-2020.text: Wohl's boulevard comedy about a divorcing elderly couple earns mixed reviews. Critics praise Alexander and Cromwell's performances but find the play derivative and sitcom-like, struggling to balance humor with depth.

west-side-story-2020.text: Van Hove's radical reimagining divides critics with its bold use of video projections and elimination of Robbins' choreography. Some praise its visceral, modern intensity and strong leads, while others find it a muddled, pretentious mess that overwhelms the story.

whos-afraid-of-virginia-woolf-2020.text: Metcalf and Everett deliver fierce performances in Albee's masterpiece, though the production occasionally feels calculated rather than truly devastating.

the-boys-in-the-band-2018.text: This acclaimed revival of Crowley's landmark 1968 play honors the original with stellar performances and sensitive direction, though some find it dated. The all-openly-gay cast brings fresh perspective to the self-loathing characters.

straight-white-men-2018.text: Critics are divided on this thought-provoking but dramatically inert family drama. While praised for smart writing, strong performances, and nuanced exploration of privilege, many find it lacks dramatic punch, meanders without clear resolution, and doesn't fully deliver on its pr

head-over-heels-2018.text: Critics are divided on this Go-Go's/Elizabethan mashup musical. Many praise its LGBTQ inclusivity, energetic choreography, and gleeful silliness, but others find the pairing of '80s pop with 16th-century prose awkward and the songs repetitive.

gettin-the-band-back-together-2018.text: Critics find this original rock musical tacky, clichéd, and unoriginal, with a forgettable score and predictable plot. However, the energetic cast and director John Rando's spirited staging win over some audiences seeking unpretentious fun.

pretty-woman-the-musical-2018.text: Critics find Pretty Woman: The Musical a glossy but bland adaptation that sticks too closely to the film, hampered by forgettable Bryan Adams songs and an outdated premise, though strong performances—especially from the leads—provide some charm.

bernhardthamlet-2018.text: McTeer delivers a commanding, tour-de-force performance as Bernhardt, but Rebeck's witty, idea-rich play is overwritten and dramatically uneven, meandering through too much talk without sufficient dramatic thrust or deeper insight.

the-nap-2018.text: Critics are divided on this British farce about snooker match-fixing: some praise Bean's witty dialogue and the colorful characters, while others find it sluggishly paced with hit-or-miss humor and problematic trans jokes that wear thin.

the-lifespan-of-a-fact-2018.text: Critics find this timely debate about truth versus narrative intellectually stimulating and elevated by a stellar trio of performances from Radcliffe, Jones, and Cannavale, though some dismiss the 85-minute play as thin or sitcom-like despite its urgent relevance.

the-ferryman-2018.text: Jez Butterworth's epic Irish family drama earns widespread acclaim as a masterpiece of storytelling, with critics praising Sam Mendes' direction and the superb ensemble cast, though some note stereotypical elements and occasional longueurs in its 3+ hour runtime.

the-waverly-gallery-2018.text: Critics praise Elaine May's extraordinary Broadway return at 86, delivering a heartbreaking, meticulously detailed performance as a woman with dementia in Lonergan's poignant memory play, though some find the work itself uneven or emotionally draining.

torch-song-2018.text: Critics praise Michael Urie's powerhouse performance and the play's enduring relevance, though some find the revival can't escape Harvey Fierstein's shadow and note uneven staging that feels both moving and dated.

american-son-2018.text: Critics praise Kerry Washington's riveting performance in this timely racial drama about a mother searching for her missing son, but find Christopher Demos-Brown's play heavy-handed and didactic, with characters that feel more like talking points than people.

king-kong-2018.text: Critics praise the spectacular 20-foot Kong puppet as a technical marvel, but find the musical surrounding it disappointing, with forgettable songs, weak storytelling, and flat characters that can't match the ape's emotional range.

the-new-one-2018.text: Birbiglia's deeply personal one-man show about reluctant fatherhood wins over critics with nonstop laughter and genuine emotion, though some find the parenting material less compelling than the setup. A winning Broadway debut that's both hilarious and moving.

the-prom-2018.text: Critics mostly embrace this big-hearted musical comedy for its infectious energy, sharp Broadway satire, and Casey Nicholaw's dazzling choreography, though some find it broad, self-congratulatory, and tonally inconsistent in balancing laughs with its LGBTQ message.

the-cher-show-2018.text: Critics are mixed on this glitzy jukebox bio-musical. While Stephanie J. Block's performance and Bob Mackie's dazzling costumes earn widespread praise, reviewers cite a shallow, rushed book that sacrifices depth for spectacle—though Cher fans will likely enjoy the campy fun.

network-2018.text: Critics praise Bryan Cranston's electrifying, tour-de-force performance as Howard Beale, but reactions to Ivo van Hove's multimedia production are mixed—some find it thrilling and relevant, others feel the tech-heavy staging overwhelms the human drama.

to-kill-a-mockingbird-2018.text: Sorkin's adaptation earns mostly positive reviews for its theatrical power and timely resonance, with Jeff Daniels' nuanced Atticus widely praised. Critics split on whether changes honor or oversimplify Lee's novel.

choir-boy-2019.text: Critics praise Jeremy Pope's charismatic lead performance and the gorgeous spiritual singing in this gay coming-of-age drama, though some find the structure uneven and characters underdeveloped. McCraney's lyrical writing resonates despite occasional pacing issues.

true-west-2019.text: Critics are divided on this revival of Shepard's classic: Hawke earns widespread praise for his fierce performance, but opinions split sharply on Dano's casting and the production's overall energy, with some finding it gripping and others tedious.

be-more-chill-2019.text: Critics are mixed on this viral sensation, with many finding the energetic pop-rock score and youthful performances appealing but the frenetic tone and uneven book problematic. Younger audiences embrace it; older critics are less convinced.

kiss-me-kate-2019.text: Critics praise this handsome revival for Kelli O'Hara's glorious vocals and Warren Carlyle's electrifying choreography, though some find Scott Ellis's direction lacks spark and the updated gender politics don't fully solve the show's dated problems.

aint-too-proud-2019.text: Critics find *Ain't Too Proud* a slick, entertaining jukebox musical elevated by thrilling performances and irresistible Motown hits, though most agree the conventional book and shallow drama can't match the music's soul.

what-the-constitution-means-to-me-2019.text: Critics hail Schreck's innovative hybrid of memoir, civics lesson, and political theater as deeply personal yet universal, praising her charismatic performance and seamless blend of humor with heartbreak, though a few find its structure loose or overly didactic.

king-lear-2019.text: Jackson's fierce, commanding performance at 82 elevates Sam Gold's uneven, gimmick-laden production. Critics praise her stamina and authority but fault the director's cluttered staging and lack of cohesion, calling it a mixed showcase for a legendary actress.

oklahoma-2019.text: Fish's radical reimagining strips away nostalgia to expose Oklahoma!'s dark undercurrents, dividing critics. Most praise the bold, contemporary vision and intimate staging, though some find it pretentious or gimmicky.

burn-this-2019.text: Adam Driver delivers an explosive, tour-de-force performance that dominates this uneven revival, but Keri Russell struggles to match his intensity, resulting in weak chemistry that undermines the central romance of Wilson's dated 1987 play.

hillary-and-clinton-2019.text: Metcalf and Lithgow deliver strong performances in this smart but slight speculative drama about the Clintons during the 2008 primaries, though critics find it lacks fresh insights and dramatic heft despite witty dialogue.

gary-a-sequel-to-titus-andronicus-2019.text: Critics sharply divide over Taylor Mac's audacious comedy: some praise Lane, Nielsen, and White's brilliant clowning and the play's bold philosophical ambitions, while others find it incoherent, self-indulgent, and too messy to land its political points.

all-my-sons-2019.text: Miller's 1947 drama receives a mostly strong revival, with critics praising powerful performances from Bening and Letts, though some find the production's traditional approach overly cautious and the play's mechanics creaky.

tootsie-2019.text: Horn's hilarious, joke-packed book and Fontana's star turn make this crowd-pleasing adaptation one of Broadway's funniest musicals, though Yazbek's forgettable score lags behind and the updated gender politics don't always land.

ink-2019.text: Graham's energetic drama about Murdoch's tabloid revolution dazzles with theatrical flair and powerhouse performances from Carvel and Miller, though some critics find it more stylish than substantive, with a second act that loses momentum.

beetlejuice-2019.text: Critics find "Beetlejuice" a visually spectacular, high-energy romp with strong performances from Brightman and cast, but note an exhausting, overstuffed book and forgettable score that prevent it from reaching its full potential.

1984-2017.text: Critics find this visceral adaptation of Orwell's dystopian classic harrowing and timely, praising its punishing intensity and immersive staging, though some question whether its brutal sensory assault overshadows the story's message.

the-terms-of-my-surrender-2017.text: Moore's anti-Trump solo show divides critics: supporters find it entertaining, funny, and empowering with strong storytelling, while detractors dismiss it as self-indulgent, rambling, and too familiar—essentially preaching to the choir rather than offering fresh theatrical insigh

prince-of-broadway-2017.text: Critics find this revue of Hal Prince's legendary career entertaining but shallow, with a stellar cast delivering memorable numbers from iconic musicals, though the weak book offers little insight into the man behind the work.

time-and-the-conways-2017.text: Mixed reviews praise Taichman's direction and strong ensemble performances, but critics split on whether the handsome production overcomes Priestley's dated dialogue, heavy-handed themes, and structure that works better as concept than drama.

m-butterfly-2017.text: Critics find Hwang's extensive rewrites and Taymor's direction diminish the original's mystery and emotional power, though Jin Ha impresses. The production feels overstuffed, talky, and lacking chemistry despite Owen's efforts.

junk-2017.text: Akhtar's ambitious 1980s finance epic earns praise for brisk pacing and smart writing, but critics find it overstuffed with characters lacking depth. The large-scale production impresses, yet many feel the familiar story offers little new insight into Wall Street greed.

the-bands-visit-2017.text: Critics hail this intimate chamber musical as a small miracle, praising Yazbek's gorgeous Middle Eastern-inflected score, Cromer's sensitive direction, and the ensemble's exquisite performances for finding profound beauty in quiet human connection.

latin-history-for-morons-2017.text: Critics praise Leguizamo's energetic performance and mimicry skills, but find the show scattershot and overlong. The politically urgent material entertains and provokes, though didactic elements feel forced and historical depth lacks focus.

meteor-shower-2017.text: Steve Martin's absurdist comedy draws laughs from a talented cast (Schumer, Key, Benanti, Shamos) but critics widely dismiss it as an overextended sketch lacking substance, coherent plot, or meaningful themes—lightweight fun that feels half-baked despite stellar performances.

the-parisian-woman-2017.text: Critics find Beau Willimon's Trump-era political drama a shallow, creaky disappointment despite Uma Thurman's Broadway debut. The play draws easy laughs from anti-Trump jabs but lacks insight, with stilted dialogue and dated plotting that fails to capture contemporary urgency.

once-on-this-island-2017.text: This radiant revival wins overwhelming praise for Michael Arden's immersive staging, Camille A. Brown's exuberant choreography, and powerhouse performances led by Hailey Kilgore, though a few critics question the story's dated elements and moral simplicity.

spongebob-squarepants-2017.text: Critics praise this vibrant Broadway adaptation for its dazzling visuals, infectious energy, and Ethan Slater's star-making performance, though some find the eclectic score uneven and the staging occasionally overstuffed.

the-children-2017.text: Critics praise Kirkwood's thought-provoking post-apocalyptic drama and the superb performances, but many find the pacing glacially slow. The play's ethical questions about generational responsibility resonate powerfully, though talky exposition tests patience.

farinelli-and-the-king-2017.text: Rylance delivers a masterful performance as the mad Spanish king, elevating a thin, meandering script. Critics praise the intimate candlelit staging and glorious baroque arias, though most find the drama itself underwhelming.

john-lithgow-stories-by-heart-2018.text: Lithgow delivers a masterful acting showcase with impressive vocal and physical virtuosity, but critics are divided on whether these two literary readings justify a Broadway evening. Many find his personal family anecdotes more compelling than the stories themselves.

escape-to-margaritaville-2018.text: Critics find this Jimmy Buffett jukebox musical a lightweight, predictable confection that plays best to devoted Parrotheads. The talented cast and breezy songs earn praise, but the corny book and sitcom-level humor leave most reviewers only mildly buzzed.

frozen-2018.text: Critics are divided on Broadway's *Frozen*: fans of the film will likely enjoy the spectacle and strong lead performances, but many find it a safe, uninspired adaptation that lacks the theatrical magic of Disney's best, with a thin story stretched over two-plus hours.

lobby-hero-2018.text: Critics praise Lonergan's sharp dialogue and stellar ensemble cast in this timely revival, though some find the pacing uneven and ending anticlimactic. Brian Tyree Henry stands out in a production that balances humor with moral complexity.

three-tall-women-2018.text: Critics hail this revival as a towering triumph, with Glenda Jackson's ferocious, commanding performance leading a trio of magnificent actresses through Albee's Pulitzer-winning masterpiece under Joe Mantello's impeccable direction.

mean-girls-2018.text: Critics find Mean Girls an entertaining but uneven adaptation that captures Tina Fey's sharp wit and benefits from energetic performances, though the forgettable score and loss of the film's satirical edge keep it from being truly fetch.

children-of-a-lesser-god-2018.text: Mixed reviews for this revival, with critics praising Lauren Ridloff's powerful, transcendent performance but finding the 1980 play dated and Joshua Jackson uneven. Production lauded for accessibility efforts, criticized for heavy-handed direction and weak chemistry.

carousel-2018.text: Critics praise Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance and Justin Peck's thrilling choreography in this handsome, gorgeously sung revival, but most find Jack O'Brien's direction plays it too safe, failing to fully address the show's dated treatment of domestic abuse.

my-fair-lady-2018.text: Critics hail Sher's sumptuous, elegantly staged revival as a crowd-pleasing triumph that honors the classic while subtly updating its gender politics. Lauren Ambrose earns raves for her transformative Eliza, though some find leads merely adequate and the production overly safe.

summer-2018.text: Critics are mixed on this jukebox musical, praising the powerhouse vocals of its three leads and Summer's iconic disco catalog, but faulting the clunky, threadbare book that fails to do justice to the Queen of Disco's life story.

travesties-2018.text: Critics hail this "sparkling," "rollicking" revival of Stoppard's intellectually dense 1974 comedy as surprisingly accessible and entertaining. Tom Hollander's tour-de-force performance and Patrick Marber's brisk direction make the wordplay dazzle.

saint-joan-2018.text: Critics are divided on this handsome but uneven revival, with many praising Condola Rashad's committed performance while finding Daniel Sullivan's direction stolid and overly talky, making Shaw's verbose play feel longer than its three-hour runtime.

the-iceman-cometh-2018.text: Washington and a strong ensemble deliver powerful performances in Wolfe's briskly paced, occasionally uneven revival. Critics praise the acting and energy but are divided on whether the production captures the play's full tragic depth.

cirque-du-soleil-paramour-2016.text: Critics find Paramour's acrobatic feats stunning but say the show fails to merge Cirque du Soleil spectacle with Broadway storytelling, resulting in an incoherent mess with a weak, clichéd plot and forgettable score.

an-act-of-god-2016.text: Critics find this comedy a one-joke premise stretched thin, with uneven material that feels more suited to sketch comedy than Broadway. Parsons and Hayes earn praise for their committed performances, but the humor proves scattershot and toothless.

motown-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find the Motown catalog irresistible but fault Berry Gordy's self-serving, clunky book for being unfocused and superficial. The talented cast delivers electrifying performances of iconic hits, making it crowd-pleasing nostalgia despite weak storytelling.

cats-2016.text: The revival earns mixed reviews, with critics praising Blankenbuehler's refreshed choreography and strong ensemble work, but questioning whether the thin plot and spectacle-over-substance approach justifies its return—and finding Leona Lewis miscast as Grizabella.

the-encounter-2016.text: Critics are divided on this technologically audacious one-man show: many praise McBurney's immersive binaural soundscape as groundbreaking, while others find the nearly two-hour story rambling and exhausting once the audio novelty wears off.

holiday-inn-the-new-irving-berlin-musica.text: Critics find this Irving Berlin musical a charming, old-fashioned diversion with spectacular tap choreography and a treasure trove of classic songs, though most agree the lightweight plot and nostalgic sensibility prioritize comfort over innovation.

oh-hello-on-broadway-2016.text: Critics find Kroll and Mulaney's curmudgeonly Upper West Side characters mostly hilarious, praising their chemistry and absurdist humor, though some feel the extended sketch wears thin and may not convert newcomers unfamiliar with the duo.

heisenberg-2016.text: Critics praise Parker and Arndt's superb performances in this minimalist two-hander, though opinions split on Stephens' slender script. Many find it a quirky, touching romance with emotional depth; others dismiss it as contrived, underwritten, and unconvincing.

the-cherry-orchard-2016.text: This revival of Chekhov's classic receives largely negative reviews, criticized as disjointed, flat, and tonally confused. While Diane Lane's performance draws some praise, most critics fault the production's muddled direction and lack of emotional depth.

the-front-page-2016.text: This star-studded revival of the 1928 newspaper comedy feels dated and overly long, with a lethargic first act. Nathan Lane's entrance 90 minutes in electrifies the production, but even his masterful performance can't fully rescue the creaky material.

falsettos-2016.text: Critics largely embrace this revival as a moving, beautifully performed production, praising Finn's score and the stellar cast. While some find the material dated or structurally flawed, most laud its emotional power and timeless themes of love and family.

les-liaisons-dangereuses-2016.text: McTeer earns widespread praise for her commanding Marquise, but critics are divided on Schreiber's Valmont and the production's lack of chemistry and erotic spark.

natasha-pierre-and-the-great-comet-of-18.text: Critics praise the show's spectacular immersive staging and inventive electro-pop score, calling it thrillingly original. However, some find the narrative uneven with expository songs that drag, noting style occasionally triumphs over emotional depth.

a-bronx-tale-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find "A Bronx Tale" a pleasant but derivative crowd-pleaser that doesn't justify its musicalization. While Nick Cordero's performance as Sonny and Menken's score earn praise, the show feels overly sentimental and lacks the depth of its film predecessor.

dear-evan-hansen-2016.text: Critics hail this heartbreaker as a bold, emotionally devastating musical with a phenomenal Ben Platt leading an exceptional cast. Pasek and Paul's score and Levenson's book earn raves, though some question the implausible plot and tidy ending.

in-transit-2016.text: Broadway's first a cappella musical earns praise for its talented cast and impressive vocal arrangements, but critics find the characters stereotypical and stories predictable, calling it charming yet lightweight.

the-present-2017.text: Blanchett dazzles in her Broadway debut, but critics find this three-hour Chekhov adaptation lethargic and overlong. Mixed reviews praise the star performances while questioning the production's pace and purpose.

jitney-2017.text: Critics hail this long-overdue Broadway premiere as a triumph, praising Ruben Santiago-Hudson's masterful direction and the exceptional ensemble cast. While some note the early work's structural flaws, most celebrate Wilson's poetic dialogue and vivid characters.

sunset-boulevard-2017.text: Critics praise Scherzinger's powerhouse vocals and commanding presence in Lloyd's stripped-down, cinematic revival, though some find the concept gimmicky and the staging relentless. Mixed reviews overall, with strong performances elevating uneven execution.

sunday-in-the-park-with-george-2017.text: Critics hail this revival as near-perfect, with Gyllenhaal and Ashford delivering luminous, emotionally transparent performances that rival the original. Though the minimalist staging divides some, Sondheim's score sounds glorious and the production achieves rare transcendence.

significant-other-2017.text: Critics find Joshua Harmon's comedy-drama about a lonely gay man watching friends marry to be funny and heartfelt, with Gideon Glick's performance widely praised, though some find the protagonist too whiny and the premise overly familiar.

the-glass-menagerie-2017.text: Sam Gold's radically stripped-down revival divides critics with its stark, minimalist approach and casting of a disabled actress as Laura. Sally Field's fierce, unvarnished Amanda earns widespread praise amid debate over the bold concept.

come-from-away-2017.text: Critics praise this heartwarming 9/11 musical for its moving celebration of human kindness and stellar ensemble work, though some find the Celtic-folk score repetitive and character development thin.

the-price-2017.text: Miller's family drama gets a solid revival buoyed by a dream cast, with Danny DeVito stealing the show in his Broadway debut. While the play feels dated and slow at times, strong performances—especially Shalhoub and DeVito—elevate the material.

miss-saigon-2017.text: Critics are split on this spectacle-driven revival: some praise the soaring score, stunning production values, and strong performances, while others find the dated material problematic, with melodramatic plotting and troubling stereotypes that time hasn't improved.

sweat-2017.text: Nottage's timely, Pulitzer-winning drama about working-class Pennsylvania earns praise for its empathetic portrayal of economic decline and superb ensemble cast, though some critics find the plot predictable and structure schematic despite its powerful emotional impact.

the-play-that-goes-wrong-2017.text: Critics are divided on this British farce about a disastrous amateur production: most praise its expertly executed physical comedy and slapstick precision, but some find the one-joke premise exhausting over two hours.

amelie-a-new-musical-2017.text: Critics find this whimsical adaptation charming but lightweight, struggling to translate the beloved film's magic to stage. Phillipa Soo earns praise, but the show feels precious and exhausting, with a workmanlike score that never quite enchants.

present-laughter-2017.text: Kevin Kline dazzles with impeccable comic timing in this stylish Coward revival, though some find the 1939 comedy creaky and plodding. The strong ensemble and witty direction mostly compensate for dated material.

war-paint-2017.text: LuPone and Ebersole deliver powerhouse performances in peak vocal form, but the forgettable score and thin, overly parallel book keep this polished, visually stunning musical about cosmetics rivals more skin-deep than substantive.

oslo-2017.text: Critics hail Oslo as gripping, intelligent political theater that transforms complex peace negotiations into riveting drama. Though long and talky at three hours, the play flies by thanks to sharp writing, masterful direction by Bartlett Sher, and a superb ensemble cast.

groundhog-day-2017.text: Andy Karl delivers a tour-de-force performance in this inventive but uneven musical adaptation. Critics praise Minchin's clever lyrics and Warchus's theatrical staging, though many find the score unmemorable and the show overlong and exhausting.

indecent-2017.text: Critics hail "Indecent" as a moving, theatrically brilliant work tracing a controversial Yiddish play's journey. Vogel's script and Taichman's direction earn widespread praise, though some find the sprawling structure overly ambitious and occasionally unfocused.

the-little-foxes-2017.text: Critics praise this "superb" and "riveting" revival, with Linney and Nixon's role-swapping as Regina and Birdie earning raves. Daniel Sullivan's direction and the strong ensemble cast shine, though some find the pacing measured and melodrama muted.

hello-dolly-2017.text: Critics hail this lavish revival as a joyous, old-fashioned spectacle with stunning production values. Midler earns raves for her magnetic star power and comic timing, though some note vocal limitations. Peters brings warmth and vulnerability to her acclaimed turn.

charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory-2017.text: Critics are divided on this Broadway adaptation, with many finding it visually inventive but dramatically hollow. Christian Borle's Wonka earns praise, but the show struggles with a sluggish first act and lacks the magic of its source material.

anastasia-2017.text: Critics give mixed reviews to this lavish spectacle, praising its sumptuous costumes and gorgeous production design but faulting an overstretched story and identity crisis between fairy-tale romance and historical drama.

six-degrees-of-separation-2017.text: Critics praise Janney's commanding performance and Guare's sharp writing in this stylish revival, though many find Cullman's direction too broad and farcical, sacrificing emotional depth for laughs in a play that remains relevant but feels somewhat dated.

bandstand-2017.text: Critics praise Blankenbuehler's spectacular choreography and the talented cast, but find the earnest WWII veteran story hampered by a predictable, clichéd book and forgettable songs that never quite match the era's standards.

a-dolls-house-part-2-2017.text: Lucas Hnath's audacious sequel earns widespread praise for its sharp, funny dialogue and thought-provoking feminist themes, with Laurie Metcalf delivering a magnetic performance that anchors this modern, irreverent take on Ibsen's classic.

amazing-grace-2015.text: Critics are sharply divided on this faith-based musical about "Amazing Grace" hymn writer John Newton. While some praise the powerful vocals and ambitious storytelling, many find the score bland and Newton's conversion from slave trader unconvincing.

spring-awakening-2015.text: Deaf West's innovative revival electrifies the Tony-winning musical by integrating ASL with hearing and deaf actors, creating a theatrically exceptional and deeply moving production that enhances the story of adolescent alienation.

old-times-2015.text: Critics praise the superb performances, especially Clive Owen's Broadway debut, in this stylishly acted Pinter revival, though many fault Douglas Hodge's flashy direction for overwhelming the play's intimate menace with distracting production elements.

fool-for-love-2015.text: Critics are divided on this Shepard revival: Rockwell and Arianda deliver committed, physical performances, but many find the Broadway venue too large, sacrificing the claustrophobic intensity essential to the play's impact.

the-gin-game-2015.text: Jones and Tyson deliver masterful performances that elevate D.L. Coburn's slight, schematic Pulitzer winner about nursing home residents playing cards. Critics praise the stars' chemistry and craft while finding the play itself dated and unsatisfying.

dames-at-sea-2015.text: Critics are split on this nostalgic tap-heavy spoof of 1930s musicals, with many questioning its Broadway relevance. While the hardworking six-person cast and exuberant choreography earn praise, dated references and repetitive numbers leave most feeling it's charming but slight.

sylvia-2015.text: Critics praise Annaleigh Ashford's winning, hilarious performance as the titular dog, calling it the main reason to see this "charming but slight" comedy. While the play is deemed thin and repetitive, Ashford's physical comedy elevates the lightweight material.

therese-raquin-2015.text: Critics find this Broadway revival a sluggish, dramatically inert production despite stunning design work. Knightley's committed performance can't overcome the lugubrious pacing and joyless melodrama that makes the show feel longer than its 2.5 hours.

king-charles-iii-2015.text: Critics praise Bartlett's audacious Shakespearean "future history" written in blank verse, with Tim Pigott-Smith delivering a riveting performance as Charles.

on-your-feet-2015.text: Critics find "On Your Feet!" a formulaic but energetic crowd-pleaser that delivers infectious Latin rhythms and dazzling choreography, though hampered by a weak, sanitized book that follows jukebox musical clichés too predictably.

allegiance-2015.text: Critics are divided on this earnest musical about Japanese-American internment, praising George Takei's Broadway debut and the important subject matter but faulting heavy-handed storytelling and formulaic music that doesn't match the gravity of its historical topic.
